explanation: s1 == s2 compares references (false: different objects), while equals() compares content (true: both contain 'Hello').
++x makes x=6, then 6+6=12, then x-- returns 6 (x becomes 5), so 12+5=17.
a >= b auto-unboxes b safely; a == b may fail if b is null (NullPointerException on unboxing); > and < have same unboxing risk.
Enhanced for-loop iterates over copies of references; reassigning s does not modify the array.
Primitive array elements default to 0; reference array elements (Integer objects) default to null.
Accessing array index 10 when size is 5 throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException (a subclass of IndexOutOfBoundsException).
x = false is an assignment expression that evaluates to false, so the else block executes and prints 'B'.
Integer values -128 to 127 are cached and reuse objects (a == b is true), but 128+ are new objects (c == d is false).
switch matches 'test', prints 'A', then falls through (no break) to print 'B', but not 'C' (default is not reached after case match without break).
The ternary operator (condition ? true-value : false-value) evaluates to y (20) because x > y is false.
